==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*speḱ-}}
From {{der|en|la|conspicuus||visible, striking}}, from {{m|la|[[conspicio|cōnspicere]]||to notice}}, from {{m|la|con-||with, together}} + {{m|la|[[specio|specere]]||to look at}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/kənˈspɪk.ju.əs/}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-conspicuous.ogg|a=US}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# [[obvious|Obvious]] or [[easy]] to [[notice]].
#: {{syn|en|apparent|evident|pointed|;|observable|perceivable|Thesaurus:obvious|Thesaurus:perceptible|}}
#: {{ant|en|inconspicuous}}
#: {{ux|en|He was '''conspicuous''' by his absence.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1928|author=Lawrence R. Bourne
|title=Well Tackled!
|chapter=7|url=http://openlibrary.org/works/OL5387037W
|passage=“No, don't,” replied the superintendent; “in fact, I'd rather you made yourself '''conspicuous''' elsewhere. Go down to the landing stage and cross to New Brighton or Wallasey—doesn't matter which—and come back. No doubt you will be seen, and reported to have gone across.”}}
# [[noticeable|Noticeable]] or [[attracting]] [[attention]], especially if [[unattractive]].
#: {{syn|en|attention-grabbing|flashy|prominent|Thesaurus:conspicuous}}
#: {{ant|en|inconspicuous}}
#: {{ux|en|He had a '''conspicuous''' lump on his forehead.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1969|author=Saul Bellow|title=Mr Sammler's Planet|publisher=Penguin Books Ltd|page=6
|passage=For his height he had a small face. The combination made him '''conspicuous'''.}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|conspicuosity|conspicuous by one's absence|conspicuous consumer|conspicuous consumption|conspicuously|inconspicuous|semiconspicuous}}
